# #3937: Patch: the AI's count of the damage that gets past its Taunts lets a big attacker break a Taunt first, and keeps the attackers a Taunt's Armor would stop
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Before it ends its turn, the practice AI counts how much damage the opponent's board could deal its hero next turn, so that it can see a lethal coming and switch a unit to Defense Position to block it. That count always sends the opponent's smallest attackers at the AI's guards first, and an attacker that would do nothing to a guard is dropped from the count instead of being kept for the hero. So the AI counts less than a sensible opponent would deal. Example: the AI is at 6 life with one unit guarding in Defense Position at 3 health, and the opponent has units with 3, 3 and 4 attack. The count sends the two 3s into the guard and only the 4 at the hero, 4 damage, so the AI feels safe and leaves its other unit in Attack Position. The opponent sends the 4 into the guard and both 3s at the hero: 6 damage, and the AI is dead. Once this is built, the count lets an attacker that can break a guard alone do it first and keeps the rest for the hero, so the AI sees that lethal and puts up a second guard.

## Why

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs:1164-1170`: `damage_past_taunts` sorts the free attackers smallest first (`free.sort_by_key(|(_, attack, may_hit_hero)| (*may_hit_hero, *attack))`) and spends them on the Taunts in that order.
- `evaluate.rs:1193-1195` and `:1271-1273`: an attacker that would fall to a First Strike Taunt, or whose hit the Taunt's Armor takes whole (`if dealt <= 0 { continue; }`), is used up from the bound list and never put back. Only the attackers never reached return to the free list (`:1282`).
- §4.2 step 3 only requires that a standing Taunt be the target (`crates/engine/src/combat.rs:546-560`); the attacking player picks the order. The function's own doc says it counts what the board could deal.
- A test pins the undercount: `crates/ai/tests/ai/position_model.rs:396-411` asserts 0 for two 1/4s and a 4/4 against a Defense Mr. Vanilla at 1 health with Armor 1, where the 4/4 sent first destroys it and the two 1s then deal 2. Its `played` helper (`:363-386`) also attacks smallest first.
- The number decides whether the AI looks for a blocking switch at all: `wall_switches` returns nothing while `face_threat` stays below the AI's life (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs:961-966`, R2976000). It also feeds the evaluation's lethal threat and `ready_gap` (`crates/ai/src/lethal.rs:203`), which the opponent model's lethal reads.

## Proposal

- Keep an attacker that a Taunt would stop whole (Armor, or a First Strike that kills it) for the next Taunt or the hero, instead of discarding it.
- Before spending small attackers on a Taunt, send the smallest attacker that destroys it alone, when there is one; otherwise go smallest first as now.
- Keep it one cheap greedy pass, with no search.
- To keep the frozen greedy baseline still, put the new order behind an evaluation-weights flag, on in the AI's weights and off in the greedy's, as `gauntlet_bars_face_attacks` is (`crates/ai/src/config.rs:366,567,843`).
- Correct the pinned test to 2 and its `played` helper to play the best order.
- Update the AI README's sentence on the threat, and add a ruling in the issue's block if the bot finds §9.9 silent.

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs` (`damage_past_taunts`), `crates/ai/src/config.rs`
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/position_model.rs`, a `wall_switches` test beside the R2976000 ones
- SPEC §9.9 and `crates/ai/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Armor test above expects 2, and a board with a 3-health Defense guard against 3, 3 and 4 attackers counts 6; both fail today.
- [ ] On that board with the AI at 6 life and a second unit in Attack Position, `wall_switches` offers switching it to Defense.
- [ ] A Taunt no single attacker can destroy is still soaked smallest first, and Reborn, Divine Shield, Trample and Poisonous keep their existing tests.
- [ ] The greedy baseline's weights leave the old order on, and its tests are unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` and `cargo jackioh gate` pass.

## Size and risks

Small to medium: one function, a flag, tests and a README line. Difficulty hard (the AI). Medium risk: the threat feeds every evaluation and one learned-evaluation input, so pinned AI fixtures and gate games may move. The gate shows whether it plays better or only differently.

## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43755376587)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`damage_past_taunts_with` now counts what the opponent's board could deal past the AI's Taunts under a better order of attackers. An attacker a Taunt would stop whole (its Armor takes the hit whole, or its First Strike destroys the attacker) waits for the next Taunt or the hero instead of being thrown away. The smallest attacker that destroys a Taunt alone goes at it first. A flag, on in `AI_EVAL` and off in `GREEDY_EVAL`, gates both changes. The pinned Armor test then counts 2, a 3-health Defense guard against 3, 3 and 4 counts 6, and `wall_switches` offers the second unit's switch at 6 life. A ruling and the README record it.

**Deviation from the issue.** The issue says "one greedy pass, send the smallest lone breaker first". I prototyped that literal rule in a scratch copy and it undercounts. A Defense Mr. Vanilla at full health (4 health, Armor 1) against attackers 2, 2, 2, 2 and 9: the literal rule counts 8, while the true best is 9 (four 2s soak it, the 9 goes face). The same happens when attackers that cannot reach the hero are free soakers. So the count is the larger of two orders, smallest first and breaker first, each one a line the opponent can play. That is two cheap passes with no search. Decision recorded under Risks.

## Steps

1. **`config.rs`.** Add the field with this doc, copying the sibling flags' pattern: "#3937, R3937000: whether `damage_past_taunts_with` (so `face_threat`, `wall_switches`, the threat and pressure terms, `ready_gap` and the learned features) counts the opponent's better order of attackers past a Taunt: the larger of smallest first and the smallest attacker that destroys the Taunt alone first, an attacker the Taunt would stop whole (Armor, or a First Strike that destroys it) waiting for the next Taunt or the hero. Off, attackers go smallest first and a stopped one is spent." Set `true` / `false` in the two consts.

2. **`evaluate.rs`, wrapper.** Rename nothing public. Keep `damage_past_taunts_with`'s signature and put this body in it:
```rust
let smallest_first = soak_past_taunts(state, defender, attacks, w, false);
if !w.best_attack_order_past_taunts {
    return smallest_first;
}
smallest_first.max(soak_past_taunts(state, defender, attacks, w, true))
```
   Then add `fn soak_past_taunts(state: &GameState, defender: PlayerId, attacks: &[(&CardInstance, i32, bool)], w: &EvalWeights, breaker_first: bool) -> i32`, whose body is the old body with the edits in step 3. Add one doc sentence to `damage_past_taunts_with` and change `face_threat_with`'s "Taunts soak the smallest first" to "Taunts soak what the opponent would spend on them": "With `w.best_attack_order_past_taunts` (R3937000) the larger of two orders counts: smallest first, and each Taunt broken first by the smallest attacker that destroys it alone, an attacker a Taunt would stop whole waiting until the Taunt is destroyed."

3. **`evaluate.rs`, edits inside `soak_past_taunts`'s loop over `stands[i]`**, in this order:

```rust
if breaker_first
    && let Some(at) = bound.iter().position(|(attacker, attack, _)| breaks_alone(state, attacker, *attack, &stands[i]))
{
    let breaker = bound.remove(at);
    bound.insert(0, breaker);
}
```
   - After `let mut bound = bound.into_iter();` add `let mut stopped: Vec<(&CardInstance, i32, bool)> = Vec::new();`.
   - Destructure `let Some((attacker, attack, may_hit_hero)) = bound.next()` (was `_`).
   - In the `falls_to_first_strike` branch, before `continue;`, add `if w.best_attack_order_past_taunts { stopped.push((attacker, attack, may_hit_hero)); }`.
   - Right after `let pierce = pierces(…)` and before the Cleave block, add `if w.best_attack_order_past_taunts && !stands[i].shield && dealt_after_armor(attack, stands[i].view.armor, pierce) <= 0 { stopped.push((attacker, attack, may_hit_hero)); continue; }`. It sits before the splash, so a waiting attacker sends no hit and no splash and cannot be counted twice. A shielded Taunt is excluded, so a weak attacker still pops the shield as before.
   - Replace the `let dealt = if pierce {…} else {…};` with `let dealt = dealt_after_armor(attack, stands[i].view.armor, pierce);` (same value). Keep the `if dealt <= 0 { continue; }` (it is reached only with the flag off).

4. **`evaluate.rs`, helpers**, placed above `falls_to_first_strike`:
```rust
/// §4.4 step 2: what a hit of `attack` deals a target with `armor`.
fn dealt_after_armor(attack: i32, armor: i32, pierce: bool) -> i32 {
    if pierce { attack } else { (attack - armor).max(0) }
}

/// Whether `attacker`'s one hit destroys `stand` alone (R3937000).
fn breaks_alone(state: &GameState, attacker: &CardInstance, attack: i32, stand: &TauntStand) -> bool {
    if stand.shield || stand.health <= 0 || falls_to_first_strike(state, attacker, &stand.unit, &stand.view) {
        return false;
    }
    let keywords = unit_view(state, attacker).keywords;
    let dealt = dealt_after_armor(attack, stand.view.armor, pierces(state, Some(attacker), None));
    dealt > 0 && (has_keyword(&keywords, KeywordKind::Poisonous) || dealt >= stand.health)
}
```
   Give `soak_past_taunts` a short doc: the old walk, with the two edits above.

5. **Tests** (next section). Then run `cargo fmt -p jackioh-ai` and fix only the new code's formatting. The prototype needed `breaks_alone`'s condition on one line.

Replace `the enemy's face damage next turn against the AI's health and the reverse, and the enemy's face-down cards` with `the enemy's face damage next turn against the AI's health and the reverse (the best order its attackers can take at the Taunts in the way, [[R3937000]]), and the enemy's face-down cards`.

8. **`spec/rulings/R3937000.md`.** Front matter: `id: R3937000`; `title: "The AI's count of the damage past a Taunt takes the opponent's better order of attackers and keeps the ones a Taunt would stop whole (issue #3937; amends R2976000)"`; `cards: "§9.9, §4.1, §4.2, §4.3, §4.4, R63, R346, R1361, R2976000, R3560007"`; `proven_in:` `crates/ai/tests/ai/position_model.rs` and `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`. Body, every `§` and `R` written as `[[…]]` links:
   - Problem: §4.2 step 3 only makes a standing Taunt the target; the attacking player picks the order. `face_threat` sent the smallest attackers first and dropped an attacker the Taunt stopped whole. At 6 life with one 3-health guard in Defense Position (Armor +1) against attackers 3, 3 and 4 it counted 4; the 4 breaks the guard alone and the 3s deal 6, so R2976000's `wall_switches` looked for no wall.
   - Rule: `damage_past_taunts_with` takes the larger of two lines the opponent can play. Line 1 is smallest first (attackers that may not hit the hero, then ascending). Line 2 is the same, but at each Taunt the first attacker in that order that destroys it alone goes first. Alone means: no Divine Shield, no First Strike that destroys the attacker, Armor read (Pierce skips it), Poisonous with any damage dealt.
   - Waiting: an attacker whose hit the Taunt's Armor takes whole (R346, R1361), or that its First Strike destroys, waits. It sends no hit and no splash (R63). It is free for the next Taunt or the hero once its Taunt is destroyed (a Reborn body binds it again) and bound for good while it stands.
   - Flag: `best_attack_order_past_taunts`, on in `AI_EVAL`, off in `GREEDY_EVAL`.
   - Rejected: the lone breaker alone (undercounts: the 2, 2, 2, 2, 9 board counts 8 against a true 9, and a Taunt free soakers could break); a search over orders (the count runs at every evaluation).
   - Not modelled: counter-damage, a choice among several Taunts, a second swing as anything but a second attack, and a Cleave attacker that attacks an armored Taunt only for its splash.
   - Public state only; no game rule, constant or hidden information.

9. **`spec/pending/3937.md`.** One paragraph: `**[[R3937000]] The AI's count of the damage past a Taunt takes the opponent's better order of attackers (issue #3937, 2026-11-15)**: …`, a three-sentence summary of step 8. It edits [[§9.9]] and amends [[R2976000]].

## Tests

All Rust, in `crates/ai/tests/ai/`. Boards use `board(setup)` (position_model.rs) and the top-of-file imports. Expected values below were produced in a scratch prototype of steps 1-4.

**`position_model.rs`, `mod soak`:**
- **Replace `played`** with the best result over every attack order (at most 5 attackers). Keep `auto_end_turn = Some(false)` (R345), the target "first enemy Taunt, else `hero-{HUMAN}`", and `act`:
```rust
fn played(state: &GameState) -> i32 {
    let mut start = state.clone();
    start.players[AI].auto_end_turn = Some(false);
    let attackers: Vec<String> = active_units_of(&start, AI).iter().map(|unit| unit.id.clone()).collect();
    best_after(&start, &attackers, state.players[HUMAN].hero.health)
}
fn best_after(after: &GameState, waiting: &[String], before: i32) -> i32 {
    let mut best = before - after.players[HUMAN].hero.health;
    for attacker_id in waiting {
        if !active_units_of(after, AI).iter().any(|unit| unit.id == *attacker_id) { continue; }
        // target_id as in the old helper, then:
        let next = act(after, AI, ActionBody::Attack { attacker_id: attacker_id.clone(), target_id });
        let rest: Vec<String> = waiting.iter().filter(|id| *id != attacker_id).cloned().collect();
        best = best.max(best_after(&next, &rest, before));
    }
    best
}
```
  Update the doc to "the most hero health the AI's units can take over every order they may attack in". `assert_soaks` stays; the other four old tests keep their numbers (they pass unchanged in the prototype).

Build `let units = active_units_of(&state, HUMAN); let attacks = [(units[0], 3, false), (units[1], 3, false), (units[2], 4, true)];`. `damage_past_taunts_with(&state, AI, &attacks, &AI_EVAL) == 4`; with `&GREEDY_EVAL` also 4.

**`search.rs`, `mod wall_switches_2976`** (it already has `VANILLA` and `switch_of`), add `r3937000_the_switch_is_offered_when_a_lone_breaker_makes_the_threat_lethal`. The scenario seed is `"search-wall-switch-breaker"`. p1: `"health": 6`, field `[{ "def": VANILLA, "position": "DEF", "damage": 1 }, VANILLA]`. p2: two `{ "def": VANILLA, "statsOverride": { "attack": 3, "health": 4 } }` and `VANILLA`. Assert `face_threat(&state, HUMAN) == 6` (4 today), `face_threat_with(&state, HUMAN, &GREEDY_EVAL) == 4`, and `wall_switches(&state, AI, &candidate_actions(&state, AI, Prices::NONE)) == vec![switch_of(&state, VANILLA, Position::Atk)]`.

- [ ] The Armor test expects 2 and the 3, 3, 4 guard board counts 6, and both fail on `main`; `wall_switches` offers the switch at 6 life.

## Risks

- **A threat that moves.** `face_threat` feeds the evaluation's lethal threat and pressure, `wall_switches`, `ready_gap` and one learned feature, so pinned expectations and gate games can move. In the scratch prototype of steps 1-4, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` failed only the `lethal.rs` test above and a `jackioh-tools` acceptance test, `ci_scope_runs_a_crates_groups_for_every_file_it_includes_from_outside_it`. That test names `e2e/artifacts/...` and `target/golden-diff` and has nothing to do with the AI, and the scratch copy had no `.git`. If it fails in the worktree too, compare it with `main` (CLAUDE.md rule 12) before touching anything. Any other pinned failure is the same kind as the `lethal.rs` one and needs the same reasoning before its number changes.
- **The gate on the prototype** passed: ai-vs-random 20/20 (17 needed), ai-vs-greedy 17/20 (10 needed), hard-vs-easy 20/20 (16 needed), 0 search panics, perf in budget. Re-run it on the real change; I measured no baseline, so it shows the AI plays well, not that it plays better.
- **Cost.** With the flag on, the Taunt walk runs twice per call (a clone of each Taunt and a few `unit_view`s). `ready_gap` and `face_threat` stay cheap beside `unit_worth`. If `cargo jackioh gate`'s perf lines look much slower, report the numbers instead of changing the design.
- **Determinism and hidden information.** Both passes read only public state, with no randomness, no clock and no new constant, so purity (rule 4) and the replay hash are untouched. `EvalWeights` is in no JSON or TypeScript file, so `apps/web/src/wire` does not move.
- **Greedy baseline.** With the flag off, `soak_past_taunts(.., false)` takes exactly the old branches: the armor pre-check and the `stopped` pushes are gated on the flag.
- **Known limit.** It is still greedy, not an optimum: a board mixing two Taunts that want different orders takes the better of the two global orders.

None that block the build. # Plan (sonnet, medium)

## Goal

`damage_past_taunts_with` now counts what the opponent's board could deal past the AI's Taunts under a better order of attackers. An attacker a Taunt would stop whole (its Armor takes the hit whole, or its First Strike destroys the attacker) waits for the next Taunt or the hero instead of being thrown away. The smallest attacker that destroys a Taunt alone goes at it first. A flag, on in `AI_EVAL` and off in `GREEDY_EVAL`, gates both changes. The pinned Armor test then counts 2, a 3-health Defense guard against 3, 3 and 4 counts 6, and `wall_switches` offers the second unit's switch at 6 life. A ruling and the README record it.

**Deviation from the issue.** The issue says "one greedy pass, send the smallest lone breaker first". I prototyped that literal rule in a scratch copy and it undercounts. A Defense Mr. Vanilla at full health (4 health, Armor 1) against attackers 2, 2, 2, 2 and 9: the literal rule counts 8, while the true best is 9 (four 2s soak it, the 9 goes face). The same happens when attackers that cannot reach the hero are free soakers. So the count is the larger of two orders, smallest first and breaker first, each one a line the opponent can play. That is two cheap passes with no search. Decision recorded under Risks.
